text:
Matt Tomkins was picked 199th overall by Chicago in 2012 and spent last season in Sweden with Färjestad BK. On Sunday he stopped 27 of 28 shots at Madison Square Garden, and Edmonton beat the Rangers 4-1 for its third straight win. Our numbers rate his night at about 1.4 goals better than the shots he faced deserved. That's goals saved above expected: how many goals a goalie kept out compared with what the quality of the chances should have let in. The one that got through was Pavel Dorofeyev's snap shot in the second period, a 40% look.

The score reads more lopsided than the game was. The Rangers had 58 shot attempts to Edmonton's 50 and 28 shots on goal to 25. Expected goals, which measure the quality of chances, were 2.92 for EDM and 2.44 for NYR. We put Edmonton's chance of winning that kind of game, over simulated replays of every shot, at 58%, so the Rangers were closer than the margin suggests. Edmonton made its chances count. Connor McDavid scored 50 seconds in, Colton Dach added two, the last on a 5% chance in the final minute of the third, and Evan Bouchard scored on the power play after setting up two earlier goals. New York's best look that didn't go in was a 41% chance for Alexis Lafrenière in the third, and Tomkins stopped it.

Edmonton has won three in a row. The Rangers are winless in four (0-4-0) and will want more from their goaltending after Dylan Garand finished a shade below expected, allowing three goals on 24 shots.
